questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is a malware? (1 mark)

(b) State and describe three types of malware. (3 marks)

(c) Describe three measures that can be taken to protect a school from malware attacks. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Malware (1 mark).** Malware (malicious software) is software written to damage a computer or a network, to disturb its operation, to steal data or to gain unauthorised access to it, usually without the knowledge of the owner.

**(b) Three types of malware (3 marks).**

- **Virus** - a program that attaches itself to a host file or program and copies itself into other files when the infected file is run; it spreads when files are shared (for example by flash disks) and can corrupt or delete data.
- **Worm** - a self-replicating program that does not need a host file; it spreads by itself through a network or by e-mail, using up bandwidth and memory and slowing down the computers.
- **Trojan horse** - a program that looks useful or harmless (a free game, a crack) but secretly does harm, for example opening a back door that lets an attacker steal data or control the computer. It does not replicate.

(Other types: spyware, ransomware, adware, keyloggers.)

**(c) Three protection measures for a school (3 marks).**

- Install **antivirus / anti-malware software** on all computers and update it regularly, with a regular scan of the computers and of the flash disks brought by students and teachers.
- Use a **firewall** on the school network and keep the **operating system and programs updated** (security patches), so that known weaknesses are closed.
- **Educate and restrict the users**: forbid the installation of unknown software and the opening of suspicious e-mail attachments or links; give each user an account with a password and limited rights; keep regular **backups** so that data can be restored after an attack.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define the term information system. (1 mark)

(b) State four components of a basic information system. (2 marks)

(c) State two factors that determine the reliability of an information system. (2 marks)

(d) Describe briefly an expert system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Information system (1 mark).** An information system is an organised set of people, hardware, software, data and procedures that collects, processes, stores and distributes information to support the operations and the decision making of an organisation.

**(b) Four components (2 marks).** **Hardware**, **software**, **data**, and **people** (the users). (Procedures and communication networks are also accepted.)

**(c) Two factors of reliability (2 marks).**

- The **quality and accuracy of the input data** (validated and verified), because wrong data gives wrong information ("garbage in, garbage out").
- The **dependability of the hardware and software** (well maintained, free from faults, with a stable power supply, backups and security against unauthorised access), so that the system is available and gives the same correct results every time.

**(d) Expert system (2 marks).** An expert system is a computer program that imitates the knowledge and reasoning of a human expert in a narrow field. It has a **knowledge base** (facts and rules given by experts), an **inference engine** that uses the rules to reach conclusions, and a **user interface** through which the user answers questions and receives advice (for example a medical diagnosis or a fault diagnosis in a car).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) State the THREE divisions of a CPU. (1 mark)

(b) Make a labelled diagram of the machine cycle. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) The three divisions of the CPU (1 mark).** The **Control Unit (CU)**, the **Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU)** and the **registers** (the small, very fast memory locations inside the CPU).

**(b) The machine cycle (2 marks).** The machine cycle (instruction cycle) is the sequence of four steps that the CPU repeats for every instruction of a program: **fetch** (the instruction is copied from the memory into the CPU), **decode** (the control unit works out what the instruction means), **execute** (the ALU carries out the operation) and **store** (the result is written in a register or in memory). Then the cycle starts again with the next instruction.
